prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Production 2D combat sprites for Mouse Frontier, matching the referenced APPROVED creature exactly: same species/anatomy, silhouette, face, proportions, palette, materials, pixel-art outline and shading. NEW authored intermediate poses, never rotations/duplicates of one picture. Transparent RGBA background, clean alpha in all gaps; no scenery, shadows, text, labels or grid. Layout EXACTLY 6 equal columns x 4 rows, 1536x1024, 24 cells256x256. ONE complete creature in every cell, 16px edge clearance, consistent scale, fixed camera and baseline. Default face RIGHT in matching three-quarter profile; a front-facing reference can retain its approved view. Animate left to right in each row. Row1 MELEE: ready, prepare/wind-up, launch, maximum strike, follow-through, recovery to ready. Row2 RANGED: ready, prepare, aim/charge, release, recoil, recover. Row3 HIT: ready, initial flinch, recoil, maximum stagger, regain balance, return ready (do NOT fall fully over in a survivable hit). Row4 DEATH: ready, buckle/weaken, begin falling, collapse, settle, motionless final downed body with closed eyes. Last row never revives or loops. No gore. No extra accessories or limbs.  CRITICAL: all 24 cells must contain a COMPLETE creature body, even at the release frame. Keep effects small and immediately beside the body; NEVER use an effect-only cell. Max body width210px and max height210px inside each256px cell.Exactly this weathered brass/brown armored SCORPION with one low segmented body, TWO big pincers, EIGHT walking legs and ONE long jointed tail arcing above body to a curved sharp stinger. Preserve every plated segment, olive-brown/brass palette and dark pixel outlines. Face right. Melee draws pincers back then snap/forward sting (tail remains attached); ranged tail makes a restrained toxic-droplet flick to right with complete scorpion still visible; hit body recoils and legs brace; death legs curl under, body settles on side and tail droops. Never add antennae, wings, extra tails or humanoid body.
